content.text: Digital creators in regions with stringent [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/payment-solutions-zimbabwean-digital-sellers-my-unfiltered-take-2|COREMERCH guide to payment]] restrictions face significant challenges in setting up functional online stores. Platforms like PayPal and Stripe are often unavailable, leaving many without viable infrastructure. COREMERCH offers two distinct stacks to address these challenges: Stack 01 utilizes GitHub Pages and Apps Script, while Stack 02 employs [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-r2-digital-product-storage-delivery-what-actually-12|Cloudflare R2]] Pages, Workers, and [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/how-supabase-order-database-digital-stores-complete-infrastructure-11|supabase]]. This comparison will clarify how these options cater to creators needing crypto payment acceptance and seamless product delivery.
What Each Option Actually Offers

Stack 01, the Sovereign Starter Stack, delivers a quick deployment of 4-6 hours following the Sovereign Blueprint. It integrates GitHub Pages for hosting and Apps Script for backend logic, making it accessible for creators familiar with these tools. Conversely, Stack 02, the Edge Commerce Stack, offers a more robust setup with Cloudflare Pages and Workers, alongside Supabase for order management. This stack is deployed end-to-end in 48 hours and includes 30 days of support, making it a compelling choice for creators looking for a more comprehensive solution.
How They Handle Restricted Countries

Both stacks are designed for creators in regions where typical payment systems fail. Stack 01's simplicity makes it favorable for those just starting, particularly in countries like Nigeria or Venezuela. However, Stack 02 stands out with Supabase's capabilities, offering a more structured environment for managing orders and user data, essential in countries facing economic instability. This structured approach can help mitigate the risks associated with financial isolation, making Stack 02 a more resilient choice for long-term operation.
Payment Speed, Fees, and Real Costs

Both stacks leverage NOWPayments for crypto transactions, ensuring low fees at 0.5% per transaction. Stack 01 requires more manual setups, potentially increasing time to transaction completion. Stack 02, with its automated processes and backend integration, promises faster payment verification and order processing. This difference becomes critical when managing multiple products and transactions, as Stack 02’s infrastructure is optimized for speed and efficiency, minimizing the impact of potential delays on revenue generation.
Complete ownership of your digital store is guaranteed post-deployment.
Ownership, Automation, and Delivery

A significant advantage of both stacks is the complete ownership of the infrastructure post-deployment. Stack 01 allows creators to manage their stores independently without recurring fees or dependencies on third-party platforms. Stack 02 enhances this autonomy by providing automated order processing through Supabase, ensuring seamless delivery of digital products. Creators can focus on their content rather than backend logistics, which is particularly beneficial when scaling operations to accommodate more products.
Which Architecture to Choose Based on Your Situation

Choosing the right architecture depends on your specific needs. If you’re a solo creator looking for a quick setup with minimal complexity, Stack 01 is a practical choice. However, if you're establishing a more extensive digital store with multiple products, Stack 02 provides a robust framework that handles increased demands and customer expectations efficiently. For creators facing financial uncertainty or seeking to optimize their operations, investing in Stack 02's capabilities can lead to significant long-term advantages.
How do I build a digital store that accepts crypto payments for free?

The difference between Stack 01 and Stack 02 is not which one works — both work — it is which one fits your situation. Stack 01 is the right choice if you want to deploy yourself, you are comfortable with Google Workspace tools, and your initial volume is under 100 orders per day. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 documents the complete Stack 01 build with full source code and step-by-step configuration. Stack 02 is the right choice if you want the deployment done for you, you need higher volume capacity, or you want email deliverability infrastructure configured from day one. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH deploy Stack 02 under your accounts in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff. Both are available at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Stack 02 offers automated order processing for efficiency and speed.
Related: How Creators Like You Are Building Sovereign Stores

The setup decision comes down to time versus depth. The Sovereign Blueprint at $47 gives you everything to build Stack 01 yourself in an afternoon or Stack 02 over a weekend — full source code, step-by-step configuration, and the NOWPayments integration guide. The Edge Commerce Stack at $197 has COREMERCH build Stack 02 for you in 48 hours, end-to-end tested before handoff, with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured for email deliverability. Both paths lead to a store you own completely. Both are at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
Your Deployment Checklist

Read the Sovereign Blueprint before you start configuring anything — understanding the complete architecture before touching any settings prevents the most common configuration mistakes. Create all required accounts first: NOWPayments, Cloudflare or GitHub, Supabase or Google account, Resend or Gmail. Then configure the backend with all credentials before deploying it. Then deploy the backend and confirm the endpoint is live. Then configure NOWPayments with the endpoint URL. Then build and deploy the storefront. Then configure your custom domain if using one. Then run the mainnet test. Then check the order database. Then — and only then — share the URL. The sequence is not arbitrary. Each step depends on the previous one.
